scripts.purpose: Shared safety, configuration, privilege, path, health-check, client-publish, and credential helpers for supported operations.
scripts.invocation: Internal library; source only from scripts/ops/*.sh.
scripts.safety: Strict shell mode, path containment, hidden secret values, temporary MongoDB config files with mode 0600, and client files published by rename with earlier hashed assets kept.

scripts.purpose: Read-only production checkout, environment, service, and readiness validation.
scripts.safety: Does not modify Git, dependencies, service state, or data and never prints secret values.

scripts.purpose: Deploy a verified production branch to the systemd-managed DeFTrack service, or roll it back to an earlier commit.
scripts.invocation: npm run ops:deploy -- --dry-run; npm run ops:deploy; npm run ops:deploy -- --expect-commit <full hash>; npm run ops:deploy -- --rollback-to <commit>
scripts.safety: Runs one deploy or rollback at a time, requires a clean checkout on the expected branch, can require an exact remote commit, uses fast-forward-only Git updates, runs checks and build before restart, builds the client beside the live one so a failed build leaves it untouched, writes no file its group could change, limits rollbacks to earlier commits, and verifies readiness.

scripts.purpose: Create compressed, complete-marker-protected MongoDB backups with bounded retention.
scripts.invocation: npm run ops:backup -- --dry-run; npm run ops:backup
scripts.safety: Uses a mode-0600 temporary MongoDB config, removes incomplete dumps, never writes into an existing backup, records a checksum of every file, runs one at a time with restores and restore checks, keeps dumps from other accounts, and restricts retention deletion to the backup root.

scripts.purpose: Restore a verified MongoDB dump after creating a safety backup.
scripts.invocation: npm run ops:restore -- --backup defcon_explorer_TIMESTAMP --dry-run; add --yes for a real restore.
scripts.safety: Requires an in-root completed backup whose checksums match and explicit --yes, creates a pre-restore backup, controls systemd state, fails unless mongorestore reports every collection restored, and verifies readiness.

scripts.purpose: Prove a backup can be restored by loading it into a throwaway MongoDB and comparing document counts.
scripts.invocation: npm run ops:restore-check -- --dry-run; npm run ops:restore-check
scripts.safety: Never reads MONGODB_URI or touches the service: it starts its own MongoDB in a private temporary folder beside the backups, listening only on a socket in that folder and on no TCP port, and removes both when it ends.

scripts.purpose: Copy finished MongoDB backups to a second host and check each copy against its checksums.
scripts.invocation: On the second host, with lib.sh beside it: backup-pull.sh --from account@host: --to PATH --ssh-key FILE
scripts.safety: Only reads from the source, accepts only exact backup names, moves a copy into place after its checksums pass, keeps copies private, fetches a bounded number per run, removes old copies by count so they stay when the source stops, and fails when the newest copy is too old.

scripts.purpose: Measure API latency, throughput, and error rate against an explicitly selected base URL.
scripts.safety: Read-only benchmark; run it only against infrastructure you operate and size concurrency for the target environment.

scripts.purpose: Measure WebSocket connection and event-delivery behavior.
scripts.safety: Read-only benchmark; run it only against infrastructure you operate and size connection count and spread for the target environment.
